items.title: Pay settlement amount to avoid lawsuit
items.quote: Überweisen Sie den Vergleichsbetrag bis zum 01.12.2026 auf das Konto IBAN DE88 3704 0044 0532 0881 00, Kontoinhaber M. Beispielmann.
items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar deadline of 01.12.2026 for the settlement payment, so no period calculation is needed; this date is simply adopted as the due date. (For reference, 2026-12-01 is a Tuesday, not a weekend/holiday, so no shifting rule under §193 BGB would apply even if it had been computed from a period.)

warnings: This is a private pre-litigation settlement demand (Abmahnung) from a law firm, not a court or authority decision; there is no official Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung and no legal obligation exists until a court establishes liability.

No concrete evidence (IP address, timestamp, screenshot of the alleged filesharing offer) is included in the letter despite the specific accusation, so the claim cannot be verified from this document alone.

It is unusual for a copyright Abmahnung to waive the cease-and-desist declaration ('Eine Unterlassungserklärung ist bei Zahlung nicht erforderlich') in exchange for payment alone; this can be a pressure tactic to obtain a quick payment without the recipient obtaining any binding assurance against future claims, and such mass-Abmahnung schemes for alleged filesharing are a known pattern for both legitimate aggressive law firms and outright scams.

The recipient should independently verify the sender's identity (law firm registration, bar membership of 'Dr. Beispielmann'), confirm the IBAN belongs to a genuine account controlled by the stated firm/client, and strongly consider consulting an independent lawyer specializing in Urheberrecht before paying anything, rather than paying under the time pressure created by the 'letzte außergerichtliche Gelegenheit' wording.

The short payment deadline (about two weeks from the letter's date, roughly one week from today) combined with a threat of legal action if unpaid is a classic pressure tactic seen in both legitimate and fraudulent Abmahnung letters and should not be accepted at face value.
